name: Bruce Springsteen
milestone_by_age_26: Released debut album 'Greetings from Asbury Park, N.J.' on Columbia Records at age 23 in January 1973.
early_history_summary: Springsteen grew up in a working-class family in Freehold, New Jersey, and began playing guitar at 13. He played in local bands through his teens, including Steel Mill, before signing with Columbia Records in 1972 and recording his debut album at 914 Sound Studios.
family_context_summary: Born to a working-class family in Freehold, New Jersey; father Douglas was a bus driver with mental health issues, mother Adele was a legal secretary and the family's main breadwinner.
primary_early_advantage_tags: jersey shore music scene, live performance reps, working-class urgency, asbury park clubs
evidence_summary: Springsteen grew up in a working-class New Jersey family and began playing guitar at 13, joining local bands as a teenager. He spent years gigging in Asbury Park clubs before signing with Columbia Records at 22 and releasing his debut album at 23. His distinctive songwriting and relentless live performance work ethic were the primary engines of his early breakthrough. No family domain advantage or financial platform was documented.
starting_point: Born to a working-class family in Freehold, New Jersey; father was a bus driver, mother a legal secretary.
current_position: Still actively touring and recording at age 76; sold music catalog for ~$500M in 2021; net worth estimated ~$650M; resides in New Jersey.

trajectory.event: Released debut album 'Greetings from Asbury Park, N.J.' on Columbia Records.
Released 'Born to Run', which became his breakthrough hit album.
Released 'Born in the U.S.A.', one of the best-selling albums of all time.
Inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame.
Headlined the Super Bowl XLIII halftime show.
Sold his entire music catalog to Sony for approximately $500 million.

name: Philippe Honoré
milestone_by_age_26: First published drawing in regional newspaper Sud-Ouest at age 16 in 1957, but this was a minor first publication, not a material career milestone; his significant work as a Charlie Hebdo staff cartoonist began in 1992 at age 50.
early_history_summary: Self-taught artist from Vichy who grew up in Pau, sold his first drawings to Sud-Ouest at 16, and worked as an industrial designer while building a long career in press cartoons.
family_context_summary: Born in Vichy; parents divorced after his birth and father died accidentally; family grocery went bankrupt forcing him to leave school.
evidence_summary: Honoré was a self-taught cartoonist who first published at 16 in a regional newspaper but did not achieve a material career milestone by age 26. His significant career as a staff cartoonist for Charlie Hebdo began in 1992 at age 50. He was assassinated in the Charlie Hebdo shooting in January 2015.

name: Thierry Sabine
milestone_by_age_26: Won France's 1974 GT series championship at age 25 and organized the first Enduro Le Touquet beach race in 1975 at age 25-26.
early_history_summary: Born to a wealthy family in Neuilly-sur-Seine, Sabine graduated in marketing and advertising from EFAP before becoming a racing driver. He won France's 1974 GT series, competed in the 24 Hours of Le Mans in 1975-76, and organized the first Enduro Le Touquet in 1975.
family_context_summary: Born to a wealthy family; father was a dentist in Le Touquet and occasional rally driver, mother was a Paris antiques dealer.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was an occasional rally driver, providing early exposure to motorsport culture.
primary_early_advantage_tags: wealthy family, father rally driver, french motorsport scene, marketing education, racing access
evidence_summary: Sabine was born to a wealthy family; his father was a dentist and occasional rally driver, his mother a Paris antiques dealer. He graduated in marketing and advertising from EFAP, then became a racing driver, winning France's 1974 GT series at 25 and organizing the first Enduro Le Touquet in 1975. Family wealth and father's motorsport involvement provided early access to racing and the financial freedom to pursue ambitious event organizing.
starting_point: Born to a wealthy family in Neuilly-sur-Seine; father was a dentist and occasional rally driver, mother a Paris antiques dealer.
current_position: Died in a helicopter crash on January 14, 1986 at age 36 during the Dakar Rally in Mali; final role: founder and main organizer of the Dakar Rally.

trajectory.event: Won France's 1974 GT series championship as a racing driver.
Organized the first Enduro Le Touquet beach race and competed in the 24 Hours of Le Mans.
Got lost in the Libyan Desert during the Abidjan-Nice Rally, inspiring the concept for the Paris-Dakar Rally.
Launched the first Paris-Dakar Rally in December 1978 with 170 competitors.
Died in a helicopter crash during the Dakar Rally in Mali.

name: Lu Li
milestone_by_age_26: Won Olympic gold medal on uneven bars with a perfect 10.0 at the 1992 Barcelona Olympics at age 15.
early_history_summary: Lu Li began gymnastics training at age 5 in Changsha, Hunan, and entered the Chinese national team in December 1991 at age 15. She won Olympic gold on uneven bars at the 1992 Barcelona Olympics with a perfect 10.0, also winning silver on balance beam.
family_context_summary: Born in Changsha, Hunan; parents enrolled her in gymnastics at age 5 to build her physical strength as she was frail and had poor appetite. Mother had some school gymnastics background.
parent_family_domain_summary: Mother had practiced school-level gymnastics and taught Lu Li basic movements like splits and stretches in early childhood, but was not a professional in the field.
primary_early_advantage_tags: chinese gymnastics pipeline, early specialization, dedicated coaching, provincial sports school, innovative routine
evidence_summary: Lu Li was born in Changsha and enrolled in gymnastics at age 5 by parents concerned about her frail health. She progressed through the Hunan provincial sports school system and entered the Chinese national team at 15. Her coaches designed an innovative uneven bars routine (the 'Lu Li salto') that earned a perfect 10.0 at the 1992 Olympics. The Chinese state gymnastics pipeline provided elite training and specialized coaching from childhood.
starting_point: Born in Changsha, Hunan, China to working-class parents; enrolled in gymnastics at age 5 to address frail health and poor appetite.
current_position: Living in the United States, coaching gymnastics alongside her husband Guennadi Komissarov; resides in California.

trajectory.event: Won Olympic gold on uneven bars with a perfect 10.0 at the Barcelona Olympics.
Won uneven bars gold at the Chinese National Games and retired due to health reasons.
Enrolled at Peking University to study international relations.
Graduated from Peking University.
Moved to the United States and began coaching gymnastics in California.

name: Mohammed Abdulla Hassan Mohamed
milestone_by_age_26: Began refereeing career in 2000 at age 22 but did not achieve a material milestone by age 26; earned FIFA badge in 2010 at age 32 and first major assignment in 2011.
early_history_summary: Emirati football referee who began his career in 2000 and gradually rose through the ranks, earning his FIFA badge in 2010 and officiating at the 2018 FIFA World Cup.
evidence_summary: Mohammed Abdulla Hassan Mohamed began his refereeing career in 2000 at age 22 but did not achieve a material milestone by age 26. His FIFA badge came in 2010 at age 32, and his first major break was in 2011. He later officiated at the 2018 FIFA World Cup.

name: Javier Solana
milestone_by_age_26: Graduated from Complutense University at 22 and joined PSOE clandestinely in 1964, but no material career milestone by age 26; his doctorate came at 29 and his political career took off after age 35.
early_history_summary: Solana studied physics at Complutense University, joined PSOE clandestinely in 1964 under Franco, and became an assistant professor at the University of Virginia at 26. His doctorate came in 1971 and his political career began in earnest in 1977.
family_context_summary: Born in Madrid to a prominent Spanish family; father was a chemistry professor who died when Javier was 19; mother died in 2005. Elder brother Luis was imprisoned for political activities under Franco.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a chemistry professor, providing an academic family environment, but not directly in physics or politics.
evidence_summary: Solana came from a prominent Spanish family; his father was a chemistry professor. He graduated from Complutense University at 22 and joined PSOE clandestinely under Franco. He became an assistant professor at UVA at 26, but this was a standard academic step, not a material career milestone. His doctorate came at 29 and his significant political career began after 1977.

name: Chico Mendes
milestone_by_age_26: Was a rubber tapper who learned to read at 18 but did not achieve a material milestone by age 26; his union organizing began around 1973 at age 28-29 and his major activism came in the 1980s.
early_history_summary: Born in a rubber reserve in Acre, Brazil, Mendes began working as a rubber tapper at age 9 and learned to read at 18 from a communist fugitive. He began organizing rubber tappers in the 1970s and became a leading environmental activist before his assassination in 1988.
family_context_summary: Born in extreme poverty in a rubber reserve in Xapuri, Acre; son of a second-generation rubber tapper; one of 17 siblings, only 6 of whom survived childhood.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a rubber tapper; no domain advantage beyond inherited poverty and labor conditions.
evidence_summary: Chico Mendes was born in extreme poverty in the Amazon rubber plantations of Acre, Brazil, and began working as a rubber tapper at age 9. He learned to read at 18 from a communist fugitive. By age 26, he was still a rubber tapper with no material career milestone. His union organizing began around 1973 and his major environmental activism came in the 1980s, leading to his assassination in 1988.

name: Mile Mrkšić
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found; his notoriety came from commanding JNA forces during the Battle of Vukovar in 1991 at age 44, for which he was convicted of war crimes.
early_history_summary: Born in Kozarac near Vrginmost in present-day Croatia, Mrkšić served in the Yugoslav People's Army and rose to colonel, commanding the 1st Guards Motorised Brigade during the Battle of Vukovar in 1991.
evidence_summary: Mile Mrkšić was born in Kozarac near Vrginmost in present-day Croatia in 1947. No material milestone by age 26 was found in reviewed sources. His notoriety came from commanding JNA forces during the Battle of Vukovar in 1991 at age 44, for which he was convicted of war crimes by the ICTY and sentenced to 20 years.

name: Ramdev
milestone_by_age_26: Studied at gurukuls through his twenties but did not achieve a material milestone by age 26; established his ashram in 1995 at age 29-30 and began large yoga camps in 2002 at age 36-37.
early_history_summary: Born Ram Kisan Yadav in a poor farming family in Haryana, Ramdev attended gurukuls from a young age, studied Sanskrit and yoga, and met his future business partner Balkrishna as a fellow student. He established the Kripalu Bagh Ashram in 1995 and co-founded Patanjali Ayurved in 2006.
family_context_summary: Born to illiterate farming parents in Alipur village, Mahendragarh district, Haryana; family was very poor; had partial facial paralysis from childhood.
evidence_summary: Ramdev was born to a poor farming family in Haryana and attended gurukuls from a young age, studying Sanskrit and yoga. By age 26, he was still a student at a gurukul with no material career milestone. He established his ashram in 1995 at age 29-30, began large yoga camps in 2002, and co-founded Patanjali Ayurved in 2006, building a multi-billion dollar empire.

name: Ljubomir Vranjes
milestone_by_age_26: Won Swedish handball championship with Redbergslids IK in 1993 at age 19, and went on to win the European Handball Championship with Sweden in 1998 at age 24.
early_history_summary: Vranjes started playing handball at age 4 at Kortedala IF in Gothenburg. At 17, he joined Redbergslids IK, a Swedish premier league team, and won his first Swedish championship at 19 in 1993. He joined the Swedish national team in 1996 and won multiple European and World championships.
family_context_summary: Born in Gothenburg to Serbian immigrant parents; father worked at Volvo. Grew up in Kortedala, a working-class suburb with social challenges.
primary_early_advantage_tags: early handball specialization, gothenburg handball hub, redbergslids IK, overcoming adversity, small stature
evidence_summary: Vranjes was born in Gothenburg to Serbian immigrant parents and grew up in a tough neighborhood. He started handball at age 4 and joined top Swedish club Redbergslids IK at 17, winning his first Swedish championship at 19. Despite his small stature (1.66m), he became a key playmaker through tactical intelligence and relentless practice. The Swedish handball ecosystem in Gothenburg and his early, sustained specialization were the primary advantages.
starting_point: Born in Gothenburg, Sweden to Serbian immigrant parents; father worked at Volvo; grew up in Kortedala, a working-class suburb.
current_position: Sporting director of SG Flensburg-Handewitt in Germany; former elite handball player and coach who won the EHF Champions League as coach in 2014.

trajectory.event: Won Swedish handball championship with Redbergslids IK.

name: Art Spiegelman
milestone_by_age_26: Co-created Wacky Packages for Topps, which became a massive commercial success in 1972-73 outselling Topps baseball cards, at age 24-25.
early_history_summary: Spiegelman began cartooning at age 12, created the fanzine Blasé at 14, and started working at Topps Chewing Gum at 17-18 under art director Woody Gelman. He co-created Wacky Packages, which became a huge commercial hit in 1972-73, and was involved in the underground comix scene in San Francisco in the early 1970s.
family_context_summary: Born in Stockholm to Polish Jewish Holocaust survivors; family immigrated to the US in 1951 and settled in Queens, New York. Father was in sales, mother committed suicide in 1968. Older brother perished in the Holocaust.
primary_early_advantage_tags: topps mentorship, art and design school, underground comix scene, early professional cartooning, holocaust survivor family
evidence_summary: Spiegelman was born in Stockholm to Polish Jewish Holocaust survivors and immigrated to Queens, New York as a child. He began cartooning at 12, attended the High School of Art and Design, and was mentored by Woody Gelman at Topps, where he co-created the commercially successful Wacky Packages. His early immersion in cartooning, mentorship at Topps, and involvement in the underground comix scene were the primary advantages. Family trauma from the Holocaust and his mother's suicide shaped his artistic direction.
starting_point: Born in Stockholm to Polish Jewish Holocaust survivors; family immigrated to the US in 1951 and settled in Queens, New York; father was in sales.
current_position: Living in New York; acclaimed cartoonist best known for Maus, which won a special Pulitzer Prize in 1992; received National Book Foundation Medal in 2022; continues to create and advocate for comics.
